subject: Human Evolution
title: Cooling Under the Sun
description: A micro-lesson that makes Cooling Under the Sun usable.

hook.text: Stand upright at noon in the tropics and only your head and shoulders face the direct sun.

buildup.text: A quadruped exposes its entire back to solar radiation—far more body surface baking in the heat.

discovery.text: Peter Wheeler calculated that bipedalism reduces sun exposure by 60%, helping avoid overheating.

twist.text: Standing also lifts the body into the breeze, improving convective cooling compared to ground level.

climax.text: Thermoregulation may not have started bipedalism, but it certainly rewarded those who stood tall.

punchline.text: Standing up was the first sunscreen.

quiz.question: How does bipedalism help with heat management?
options: It reduces sun-exposed body surface by 60%
